events.title: Storytime with Julia Moss
events.description: Join us for a special storytime with author Julia Moss as she shares her debut picture book, Wanderers: A Walk Through Time and Transportation. Since the beginning we've been on the roam. Searching for food, adventure, and home… Set off on a journey through history and see how many ways humans have dreamed up to travel. First, there was walking, camel-riding, and canoes. Then, the invention of the wheel brought bikes, trains, and automobiles. Next, we took to the air with airplanes and rockets, and now there are new breakthroughs in sustainable travel every day. And what's at the heart of each advancement? Human curiosity and inventiveness.
events.blurb: Hear author Julia Moss share her debut picture book, Wanderers: A Walk Through Time and Transportation, at a Sunday morning storytime.

events.title: Hilo: The Holiday Special with Judd Winick
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Judd Winick to the store to celebrate the Hilo Holiday Special! Judd will talk about the latest adventure in his bestselling Hilo series, take questions from the audience, and then sign books. This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of Hilo: The Holiday Special from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. The decorations are up! The gifts are wrapped! And Hilo and the gang are enjoying some holiday togetherness. Sure, it would be better if the skating pond wasn't blocked off. And if someone wasn't stealing trees from the tree lot. AND if a giant, super grumpy snowman wasn't going around destroying things. But what's a holiday without holiday surprises?! Can Hilo and friends figure out what the snowman wants before D.J.'s big family party?! Packed with family and food, love and laughter (lots of laughter!) — gather around and enjoy all the gifts of the season with Hilo!
events.blurb: Hear Judd Winick talk about the latest adventure in his Hilo series, ask him questions, and get books signed.

events.title: Storytime with Seina Wedlick
events.description: Join us as we welcome local author Seina Wedlick back to the store to celebrate her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller, about a girl who fills the starry, moonlit sky with magical tales. Every night, Noor listens for the sound of the gong and the storyteller's drum. Gong, Gong, Gong! Tap! Tap! Tap! With each beat, fantastic tales swirl and sway and unfold around her. One night, she waits and waits, but no drumbeat comes her way. Can Noor tap the drum and keep the storyteller's magic alive? Find out in this modern fairy tale about a young Nigerian girl who taps stories on her drum and carries tradition in her heart.
events.blurb: Meet local author Seina Wedlick at Linden Tree Books and hear her read from her new picture book, Noor and the Storyteller.

events.title: Book Launch with Nathan Hale
events.description: We are incredibly excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author-illustrator Nathan Hale to the store to celebrate the launch of Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales: The Web of War! Nathan will talk about the latest adventure in his bestselling Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales series, take questions from the audience, and sign books. This event is free, but you must purchase a copy of The Web of War from Linden Tree to enter the signing line. Books can be purchased with an event ticket, in person at Linden Tree, or on our website. In the summer of 1944, the Allied forces carried out the largest seaborne invasion in military history. American, British, and Canadian soldiers took to the skies and the sand, bombarding the beaches of Normandy, France, in the famous operation known as D-Day. This pivotal battle turned the tides against the Nazis, but how did the French find themselves overtaken by enemy forces to begin with? How did Hitler and his Nazi ideology sweep through Germany so quickly? And how did American military service members and civilians, from generals, to war correspondents, to heroic Black soldiers, work together to defeat the Nazi government and bring an end to Hitler's reign of terror? In The Web of War, history is in your hands! Pick your path and unravel the thrilling, shocking, gruesome, and true stories of the Second World War in this all-new hazardous tale.
events.blurb: Meet author-illustrator Nathan Hale at the launch of Nathan Hale's Hazardous Tales: The Web of War at Linden Tree Books.

events.title: I Am Human: Storytime + Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Calling All Humans! Join author-illustrator Laura G. Lee for a special I Am Human book launch, storytime, and creative workshop. Laura will begin with a reading of I Am Human and a playful conversation inspired by the book: What does it mean to be human? How are we different from AI—and how do we know? After the reading, participants are invited to join a hands-on writing and drawing workshop, responding to creative prompts through words and pictures, enjoying snacks, and sharing ideas. All ages are welcome. The workshop is especially well suited to older elementary kids, teens, and adults, while younger children are welcome to enjoy the story time portion with their families. Workshop RSVPs are encouraged so we can prepare enough materials.
events.blurb: Hear Laura G. Lee read I Am Human, then join a playful conversation about what it means to be human.

events.title: Book Launch with Lily Berlin Dodd — In conversation with Misa Sugiura
events.description: We're excited to welcome New York Times bestselling author Lily Berlin Dodd back to the store to celebrate the launch of the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series, The First Flame! Lily will be in conversation with author Misa Sugiura. With Eva locked away in Byrdhaven and Rubi missing, all Dusty can do is avoid capture and (attempt to) sleep through his nightmares in the wake of Cal's death. When fate leads Dusty back to the Lockwood Inn, he overhears the next stage of Eoin Parnassus' sinister plans for aerimanders, and knows he must do everything in his power to stop it. Dodging strict nuns, wanted posters, seasickness, altitude sickness, a clockwork army, and a perilously evil clown on the way, Myrnie, Eva, and Dusty are willing to fight to the ends of the Earth--or at least the edges of their map--to stop Eoin Parnassus, Director of Kingdom Secrets. But Rubi is hiding a shocking truth and Parnassus may pose an even bigger threat than they could ever have imagined. Who can be trusted when secrets lurk around every corner of the Kingdom?
events.blurb: Hear Lily Berlin Dodd talk with author Misa Sugiura about The First Flame, the second book in her Aerimander Chronicles series.

events.title: Storytime with Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon
events.description: Join us as we welcome Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon to celebrate their empowering new picture book, No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her journey to finding her voice, independence, and freedom on a skateboard. Kanya Sesser was born without legs, but that doesn't mean she has limits! Sometimes I still fall. But I never give up. I make things work for me. Because I'm strong. Because I'm free. Because I have NO limits. Kanya Sesser has spent her life sharing the message that no matter what life deals you, you can do anything. In this picture book based on her childhood, she tells the story of how she first learned to stand up for herself, both on a skateboard and in life. When people grab her wheelchair, to push her to class or onto the bus after school, she's too shocked and too sad to say no. The people around her don't understand that she moves herself. But when she rides a skateboard for the first time, she experiences a new sense of freedom and joy, and she finally finds her voice.
events.blurb: Meet authors Kanya Sesser and Nisha Lamsam Ligon at Linden Tree Books and hear their picture book No Legs, No Limits, inspired by Kanya's childhood and her skateboarding journey.

events.title: Middle Grade Book Club: The Wish Ring Cipher
events.description: It's the next meeting of our middle grade book club for ages 9+! The club is led by bookseller extraordinaire Lorilee. We hope to introduce interested readers to amazing new books and the opportunity to talk about them in a fun, relaxed group setting. This month's book is The Wish Ring Cipher by Alexandra Ott, a fast-paced adventure novel filled with puzzle-solving, a hint of magic, and new school fears. Please email lorilee@lindentreebooks.com to RSVP. Emma Avery has always loved solving puzzles and codes, and now that she's processing a recent autism diagnosis and facing down seventh grade at a new school, they're even more important to her. Then Emma meets Nate Lin. He's popular and funny and... loves codes, too. He introduces Emma to the Codebreakers, a group of his friends dedicated to cracking codes that have been discovered in the ruins of a nearby ghost town, which are believed to lead to magical objects. But they're not the only ones on the hunt, and when their sinister rivals close in on an object that grants unlimited wishes, the Codebreakers must race to beat them to it before they use it for dark magic.
events.attendanceNote: For readers ages 9 and older. Email the bookstore to RSVP using its events calendar.
events.blurb: Talk about The Wish Ring Cipher with fellow readers ages 9 and up at a middle grade book club led by bookseller Lorilee.

events.title: Facing Reality Without Losing Your Peace of Mind

events.title: Vietnamese Storytime & Craft / Kể chuyện và làm thủ công bằng tiếng Việt
events.description: Thân mời các bé cùng cha mẹ hoặc người chăm sóc bé đến tham dự Giờ Kể Chuyện và làm thủ công bằng tiếng Việt tại Thư Viện Evergreen! Chúng ta sẽ cùng nhau nghe kể chuyện, hát ca và tham gia các hoạt động vui nhộn giúp bé phát triển kỹ năng ngôn ngữ và niềm yêu thích đọc sách từ sớm. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Chương trình phù hợp với trẻ em ở mọi độ tuổi và là dịp tuyệt vời để cả gia đình cùng học hỏi, vui chơi và kết nối. Không cần đăng ký trước. Hãy rủ bạn bè cùng tham gia nhé! Join us for a fun and engaging Vietnamese Storytime and Craft at Evergreen Library! Children and their parents or caregivers will enjoy stories, songs, and playful activities in Vietnamese that help build early language and literacy skills. Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! This program is perfect for children of all ages, a wonderful opportunity for families to learn, play, and grow together. No registration is required. Bring your friends to join us!

events.title: Asistencia tecnológica y ayuda personalizada
events.description: ¿Estás cansado de no poder hacer cosas tecnológicas por ti mismo? ¿Cansado de esperar a que los miembros de tu familia te ayuden o hagan las cosas por ti? ¡Ahora puedes aprender a hacer todo eso por ti mismo! Tenemos personas pacientes y serviciales disponibles para ayudarte a aprender cualquier tema relacionado con la tecnología. Nunca es tarde para aprender a usar la tecnología. ¡Solo llámanos! La biblioteca te brindará apoyo para: Abrir una cuenta de correo electrónico; Conectarse a un hotspot/Wifi; Usar Chromebooks/computadoras; Usar Zoom; Encontrar e inscribirse en clases de la biblioteca; Obtener una tarjeta de la biblioteca; Reservar materiales; Usar aplicaciones de la biblioteca; Teléfono móvil; Buscar en internet. Este es un programa presencial organizado en la Sucursal de la Biblioteca Latinoamericana. El personal de la biblioteca o un voluntario estarán allí para guiarte en todo, pero serás tú quien controle la computadora. Si no puede asistir a su cita, llame y cancele. Se dará prioridad a los clientes que no falten a sus citas. Gratis. Se requiere registro. Para registrarse, llame al (408) 294-1237.
events.blurb: Practice doing tech tasks yourself with personalized, Spanish-language help at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana, so you can stop waiting on family for help.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club: Beginning (Tiếng Việt)
events.description: Xây dựng kỹ năng giao tiếp với những người học trình độ mới bắt đầu khác trong một môi trường chào đón và tôn trọng. Khóa học này sẽ sử dụng Confidence and Connections và Mango Languages. Sử dụng tài nguyên điện tử này miễn phí với thẻ thư viện. Mỗi buổi học được hướng dẫn bởi nhân viên thư viện có thể nói được tiếng Việt. Miễn phí. Phải đăng ký và làm bài kiểm tra xếp lớp. Build conversation skills with other beginner-level adult learners in a welcoming and respectful environment. This course will use Confidence and Connections and Mango Languages. Use this e-resource for free with a library card. Each session is led by library staff who can speak Vietnamese. Free. Registration & placement testing required.
events.blurb: Practice beginner English conversation skills with fellow learners in Vietnamese at Seven Trees Library.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Berryessa Branch Library presents an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Are you looking for a place to practice your English conversation skills in a fun, welcoming and safe environment? Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice your English conversation skills with other learners in a welcoming club setting.

events.title: Cricut Open Lab
events.description: The Cricut Open Lab is a 45-minute learning session on select Fridays with machines available to use. First-time users can learn what the Cricut machine is and how it works. You can also watch these tutorial videos ahead of time to get a better idea of how to use the Cricut machine and Design Space. For those who already have experience using Cricut, they are welcome to register to use a machine independently to cut out their designs. We will have Cricut machines (Explore/Air and Maker), limited supplies, and several designs available for participants. Individuals or groups up to 3 people can register for the program. Registration required. This program is generously sponsored by the Friends of the Vineland Branch Library.
events.blurb: Try out the library's Cricut machines and learn the basics in a 45-minute open lab session.

events.title: Asistencia para Búsqueda de Trabajo
events.description: ¿Buscas apoyo para avanzar en tu carrera? ¡Estamos aquí para ayudarte! Ofrecemos asistencia gratuita en: Creación de Resume y Carta de Presentación - Destaca tus habilidades y experiencia con documentos profesionales que abran puertas. Búsqueda de Oportunidades de Empleo - Te guiamos para encontrar vacantes en los principales sitios web de trabajo. Llenado de Formularios de Solicitud - Incluye ayuda con verificación de historial laboral, y otros documentos esenciales para tu contratación; Técnicas y Consejos para Entrevistas - Aprende cómo responder con confianza, qué decir, qué evitar y cómo causar una excelente impresión. Práctica para el Examen Escrito de Manejo - Prepárate con materiales y preguntas de práctica para aprobar tu examen.
events.attendanceNote: De martes a sábado. Por cita únicamente. Por favor contactar a Marlene Sanchez por correo, marlene.sanchez@sjlibrary.org o teléfono, 408.808.3033 para agendar su cita.
events.blurb: Get free job search help at Hillview Library, including support with building a resume and cover letter.

events.title: Mandarin / English Bilingual Family Storytime
events.description: Join us for stories, songs, a flannel board story, fingerplay, and a craft project with a children's librarian in Mandarin and English. For children and their caretakers. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Sing songs, hear stories, follow a flannel board tale, and make a craft with a children's librarian in Mandarin and English.

events.title: Halloween Trivia Contest
events.description: Win a $25 gift card to Target by winning a trivia contest on all things Halloween! If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Test your Halloween knowledge on movies, shows, and traditions in a trivia contest for a prize.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a volunteer. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our volunteers will listen to children read and provide support in phonics, sight words, and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the West Valley Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating children.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating children.
events.blurb: Pair up with a volunteer for one-on-one reading practice designed for grades K-3.

events.title: Family STEAM
events.description: Drop in every Saturday for a new STEAM adventure, from robots to engineering to science to making. October 31 - Robot Trick-or-Treat; November 7 - Outer Space Samples for Native American History Month; November 14 - LEGO Challenge; November 21 - Fibonacci Mosaics; November 28 - Canceled for Thanksgiving. Recommended for ages 4 and up with adult help, and 8 and up solo. Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.attendanceNote: Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket. Space is limited - tickets available at the desk 30 minutes in advance.
events.blurb: Drop in on a Saturday afternoon for hands-on STEAM activities spanning robots, engineering, science and making.

events.title: Everyone Can Code: Rock, Paper, Scissors Using Swift Playgrounds
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Create your own rock, paper, scissors game using Swift Playground! Everyone Can Code is a beginner's course on using iPads to code and modify technology, such as online games. Students will be learning the basics of coding and implementing them through the modification of rock, paper, scissors. Everything needed for this course will be provided, but you are more than welcome to bring your own personal iPad with the free Swift Playgrounds app downloaded, especially if you want to save your work. Free. Registration is recommended. This series is taught in English only. Registration closes at 12 PM the day before class. However, if seats are still available, students in grades 3-6 can walk in on Saturday if they arrive before 3 PM to sign in. Maximum class size is 25. Although the class is scheduled from 3-4:30 PM, students who finish their projects early are welcome to leave early. Todos pueden programar: Piedra, papel o tijera con Swift Playgrounds: ¡Crea tu propio juego de piedra, papel o tijera usando Swift Playgrounds! Sábado 31 de octubre de 2026 de 3 a 4:30 horas. 'Todos pueden programar' es un curso para principiantes que enseña a utilizar iPads para programar y modificar tecnología, como los juegos en línea. Los estudiantes aprenderán los conceptos básicos de la programación y los pondrán en práctica modificando el juego de piedra, papel o tijera. Todo lo necesario para este curso será proporcionado, pero puedes traer tu propio iPad personal con la aplicación gratuita Swift Playgrounds descargada, especialmente si deseas guardar tu trabajo. Gratis. Se recomienda registrarse con anticipación. Esta serie será enseñada únicamente en inglés. La inscripción cierra a las 12 p.m. el día antes de la clase. Si quedan espacios disponibles, los alumnos de grado 3 a 6 pueden venir el sábado e inscribirse antes de las 15:00 p.m. La clase tiene un cupo máximo de 25 alumnos. Aunque la clase está programada de 3-4:30 p.m., los alumnos que terminan sus proyectos antes podrán retirarse si lo desean. Everyone Can Code: Trò Chơi Kéo-Búa-Bao với Swift Playgrounds Thứ Bảy, ngày 31 tháng 10 năm 2026 từ 3-4:30 giờ chiều Hãy tự tạo trò chơi Kéo-Búa-Bao cho riêng quý vị bằng Swift Playgrounds! "Everyone Can Code" là khóa học dành cho người mới bắt đầu, hướng dẫn cách sử dụng iPad để lập trình và sửa đổi kỹ thuật công nghệ, chẳng hạn như trò chơi trực tuyến. Học viên sẽ học những kiến thức lập trình cơ bản và áp dụng chúng thông qua việc sửa đổi của trò chơi Kéo-Búa-Bao. Mọi thứ cần thiết cho khóa học này sẽ được cung cấp, nhưng bạn hoàn toàn có thể mang theo iPad cá nhân của mình với ứng dụng Swift Playgrounds miễn phí đã tải xuống, đặc biệt khi bạn muốn lưu tác phẩm của mình. Miễn phí. Xin vui lòng ghi danh trước. Lớp học được chỉ dạy hoàn toàn bằng tiếng anh. Thời hạn ghi danh kết thúc vào 12 giờ trưa ngày trước khi lớp học bắt đầu. Tuy nhiên, nếu vẫn còn chỗ trống, học sinh lớp 3-6 có thể đến trực tiếp vào thứ Bảy nếu đến trước 3 giờ chiều để điểm danh. Lớp học tối đa là 25 học sinh. Mặc dù lớp học được lên lịch từ 3 đến 4 giờ 30 chiều, nhưng học sinh nào hoàn thành bài tập sớm có thể về sớm.
events.blurb: Build your own rock, paper, scissors game on an iPad using Swift Playgrounds in this beginner coding session.

events.title: 1 on 1 Tech Assistance
events.description: Do you need to brush up on your computer skills? Whether you need assistance putting together a Word document, Excel spreadsheet, or PowerPoint presentation, submitting an online job application or other government document, or learning a new online tool, our experienced and dedicated tech tutors can help! Current Weekly Schedule: Wednesdays at 4:00 PM (in the Internet Cafe); Thursdays at 11 AM - assistance available in English or Mandarin Chinese (in the Group Study Room); Saturdays at 10 AM (in the Group Study Room). How To Attend: Participants are encouraged to pre-register; however, drop-ins are also considered.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one help brushing up on your computer skills at Willow Glen Library.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K-3 and will be held in the Reading to Children corner, within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your child to hear a volunteer read aloud in a small group at Berryessa Library.

events.title: Halloween Glitter Globe Craft
events.description: First-come, first-served. Supplies are limited. Children can enjoy making their own Halloween glitter globe craft. Please note that each child must be in attendance (and 1 craft per child) for the craft. (This is a drop-in activity or a grab-and-go craft.) The craft takes about 15 to 20 minutes to assemble. Please note the Halloween glitter globe is much smaller than the enlarged photo. Size: 2 1/2". Material: Includes self-adhesive foam pieces, glitter and plastic globes. (Recommended ages 5 years and up due to small parts). Free, with limited supplies. Other events your child can participate in at this branch: Halloween Booktacular Giveaway - front desk; Halloween Scavenger Hunt - children's area.
events.attendanceNote: First-come, first-served. Supplies are limited.
events.blurb: Make a Halloween glitter globe at Bascom Library with a drop-in craft for kids, one per child while supplies last.

events.title: Halloween Storytime & Costume Parade
events.description: Embark on a thrilling adventure during our Halloween storytime at the library, where children immerse themselves in spooky tales and festive fun. Join us for interactive storytelling, creating a bewitching atmosphere that ignites imagination and celebrates the season's magic. Costumes are encouraged. After our storytime, we'll walk around the library to show off our cool costumes. Free. There will be no Storytime B for this event. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Hear spooky stories and join a costume parade at Educational Park Library's Saturday morning Halloween storytime for children.

events.title: ELL Conversation Club for Mandarin Speakers
events.description: Join us for an in-person adult English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club. Our English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Club offers a respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English speaking & conversation skills used in everyday settings. All levels of English-speaking skills are welcome! The presenter is bilingual in both English and Chinese Mandarin. Other English language learners are welcome. Free. No registration required.

Starts: August 15, 2026; Meets: Saturdays; Instructor: Annalisa Hernandez. Free. Aprende lectura, escritura, expresión oral y comprensión auditiva de manera gratuita. Esta clase se reúne en persona en la Biblioteca Hillview Branch y está dirigida por una instructora certificada de inglés en colaboración con el Centro de Educación para Adultos Overfelt, sin costo alguno. Inicio: 15 de agosto de 2026; Días: sábados; Instructora: Annalisa Hernández. Gratis.
events.blurb: Build basic English reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills in a free in-person class led by a certified English instructor.

events.blurb: Bring your child to Alviso Library for one-on-one reading time with a volunteer.

events.title: ESL Workforce Development Workshop - Day 5: Present Yourself with Confidence
events.description: Join us for a five-session workshop designed for ESL learners who want to strengthen their workplace communication skills. In addition, participants will develop basic digital skills by learning how to use Google Workspace tools (Docs, Slides, and Drive) and Canva to create professional documents and presentations that can support job searches, interviews, and career advancement. Participants should be able to communicate in basic English (speaking, reading, and writing). Workshop Topic: Present Yourself with Confidence. This is a free program. Registration is required. Talleres de Desarrollo Laboral para Estudiantes Hispanos de ESL: Acompáñenos a este taller de cinco sesiones diseñado para estudiantes de inglés (ESL) que desean fortalecer sus habilidades de comunicación en el entorno laboral. Además, los participantes desarrollarán habilidades digitales básicas al aprender a utilizar las herramientas de Google Workspace (Docs, Slides y Drive) y Canva para crear documentos y presentaciones profesionales que les apoyen en la búsqueda de empleo, las entrevistas y el desarrollo de su carrera profesional. Los participantes deben tener la capacidad de comunicarse en inglés a un nivel básico (hablar, leer y escribir). Tema del taller: Preséntese con Confianza. Este programa es gratuito. Es necesario registrarse.

events.title: Crafternoon for Adults, Tweens and Teens
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Come unwind and learn something new at our monthly crafternoon! No experience is necessary. Supplies will be provided, and you're welcome to bring any of your own. In fact some of these crafts may benefit from your personal stash! The activities will be suitable for ages 10 and up. We will have project samples each day to help you visualize the end result. Programs will be on the fourth Sunday of the month. • October – Cardboard Nicho. Recommended items to bring: small images of a cherished item, symbol, memory, or a loved one you miss. • November – Embossing Aluminum Food Charms. Recommended items to bring: colorful Sharpies. • December – Felt and Beaded Patches. Recommended items to bring: old jewelry you don't mind disassembling, beads, colorful thread, loose buttons, scraps of fabric and lace. ¡Ven a relajarte y a aprender algo nuevo en nuestra tarde mensual de artesanías! No se necesita experiencia. Se proporcionarán los materiales, pero puedes traer los que quieras. De hecho, ¡algunas de estas artesanías pueden beneficiarse de tus propios materiales! Las actividades serán aptas para mayores de 10 años. Cada día tendremos ejemplos de proyectos para ayudarte a visualizar el resultado final. • Agosto – Paisaje de playa en collage • Septiembre – Pintura de hongos • Octubre – Nicho de cartón. Materiales recomendados para traer: imágenes pequeñas de un objeto preciado, un símbolo, un recuerdo o un ser querido al que extrañas. • Noviembre – Dijes de aluminio con relieve. Artículos recomendados para traer: marcadores Sharpie de colores, piensa en cuál es tu comida reconfortante. • Diciembre – Parches de fieltro y cuentas. Artículos recomendados para traer: joyas viejas que no te importe desarmar, cuentas, hilo de colores, botones sueltos, retazos de tela y encaje.
events.blurb: Make crafts alongside other adults, tweens and teens at the East SJ Carnegie Library, with no experience necessary and supplies provided.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Throughout this 30-minute session, our trained volunteer or a staff member of the library will not only read to your kids but also engage with them using music, felts and finger plays. As a result of participating in Reading to Children, your child will develop imagination and love of books and reading. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Bring your kids to a 30-minute reading session led by a trained volunteer at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Language and Culture Swap
events.description: ¿Hablas español y quieres aprender inglés? Speak English and want to learn Spanish? Build community with people from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. Everyone has something to contribute! Construye comunidad con personas de diferentes antecedentes lingüísticos y culturales. ¡Todos tienen algo que aportar! In this program, Spanish-proficient participants with limited English skills will share their linguistic and cultural knowledge with English-proficient participants with limited Spanish skills and vice-versa to create a mutually enriching learning experience. En este programa, los participantes con dominio del español y habilidades limitadas en inglés compartirán sus conocimientos lingüísticos y culturales con participantes con dominio del inglés y habilidades limitadas en español, y viceversa, para crear una experiencia de aprendizaje mutuamente enriquecedora. Free. Registration requested but not required.
events.blurb: Swap English and Spanish conversation with neighbors building cross-cultural friendships at Alum Rock Library.

events.title: Music and Movement
events.description: Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.blurb: Sing songs, say rhymes and move together with your whole family at Santa Teresa Library, with early literacy activities for mixed ages.

events.title: Reading Buddies with Kristina
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Children in grades K to 5 will discover the joy of reading while improving their reading skills through practice with Kristina on Saturdays. Our reading buddy will listen to children and help them build confidence in their ability to read. They will ask questions about the books being read to encourage reading comprehension. Children will enjoy one-on-one interaction with Kristina who has been trained to create a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers. Reading Buddies are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.attendanceNote: Reading Buddies are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
events.blurb: Bring a child in grades K-5 to read aloud with Kristina and build reading confidence one on one.

events.title: Citizenship Study Group (In-person)
events.description: Free. Register for reminders. Drop-ins welcome. What We Do: Outline the naturalization process; Review civics (2008 & 2025); Practice reading & writing; Analyze the interview questions; Provide references & resources; Mock interviews (depending on availability). Due to legal reasons, we cannot help you fill out the application, but we can direct you to the proper services. The class is offered in English with limited Vietnamese and Spanish assistance. For additional resources, please review our Citizenship and Immigration page.
events.blurb: Review civics questions, practice reading and writing, and run through mock interviews for the naturalization process.

events.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines as a Branch Buddy
events.description: Every now and then, libraries need a little extra love from the communities they serve. Ginger has tried and failed to escape the egg farm run by Mr. and Mrs. Tweedy, but ends up being caught and thrown into the coal bin time after time. But when Rocky the Flying Rooster arrives, there is hope that all the chickens will learn the tools to escape before being turned into chicken pot pies! events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7]; Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

Chúng tôi mong muốn mời cả gia đình cùng tham gia vào các hoạt động này để cùng hát các bài đồng dao, cùng vận động ngón tay và cùng nhảy múa vui vẻ. Âm nhạc và nhảy múa là một trải nghiệm thú vị và giúp cho cả gia đình tương tác tốt hơn, thúc đẩy niềm vui học tập cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi. Mọi người đều được nhiệt liệt chào đón tại chương trình này. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Thứ Sáu hằng tuần có hoạt động kể chuyện và thủ công tiếng Việt; riêng thứ Ba tuần thứ tư hằng tháng sẽ có chương trình kể chuyện song ngữ đặc biệt. Chương trình hoàn toàn miễn phí và không cần phải đăng ký trước.

events.title: After-School STEaM
events.description: Drop in on Tuesday afternoons at 4:30 p.m. for a new STEaM adventure every week. Active engagement with STEaM promotes academic success. The topic list is subject to change; please check back or call the branch for up-to-date details. Suggested ages vary; please refer to individual program descriptions. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Aug 18 - The Science of Soap: Floating Drawing & Pepper Experiment. Participants will learn about the properties of soap, how it cleans and why that's important by creating their own floating drawings and playing with adhesion and repulsion properties of pepper and soap. Aug 25 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Please note that the Mental Math: Multiplication program has been rescheduled for Sept 22 and the other math topics have moved accordingly. Sept 1 - Marble Run Fun. Harness the force of gravity as you create your own marble run. Sept 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge (please note topic change). In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up. Volcanoes (will be rescheduled at a later time). Learn about the different types of volcanoes and create your own eruption with common household ingredients. Sept 15 - Spike Robotics Code Quest. Learn to code a pre-built Lego Spike robot to move around and collect components using a block-based coding language similar to Scratch. Sept 22 - Mental Math: Multiplication. Children have the opportunity to learn and practice multiplication skills with a focus on understanding how multiplication works and is related to addition. Oct 6 - Wind Turbine Engineering. In this hands-on workshop, participants will build their own working wind turbines using everyday household items. Through fun, interactive experiments, they will test different designs and observe the impact of tweakable variables on performance. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Oct 13 - Paper Rockets Learn what makes rockets fly high and far! Then join us in making a rocket of your own that can fly the furthest! Participants will learn about propulsion, then create their own rockets. Oct 20 - Properties of Water (Science from Scientists). Participants will explore cohesion, adhesion and surface tension through a series of simple activities that encourage them to investigate and make observations about the unique properties of water. Free, with limited capacity. Tickets will be distributed starting 60 minutes before the program. Children younger than age 9 must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this program. Oct 27 - TBA; Nov 3 - Learn About Aerodynamics Through Paper Planes. In this high-flying workshop, participants will build different types of paper planes and learn concepts of aerodynamics and the impact of plane design through fun and interactive experiments. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Nov 10 - Ozobot Maze Runner. Teach your Ozobot to navigate a maze using simple color codes. Nov 17 - Logic Games. Work individually or in teams to solve a variety of logic puzzles. Nov 24 - TBA; Dec 1 - Let's Build Parachutes. In this workshop, participants will build parachutes of different shapes, sizes and materials, and observe the impact of their design. They will participate in fun parachute drops with different loads while learning the science behind parachute design. Lesson by Nurturing Young Mindz Foundation. Dec 8 - Lego Engineering Challenge. In this workshop, children will be encouraged to build and solve problems. Children will learn to brainstorm and build with Lego bricks, and then to redesign and build as they face challenges. For children ages 5 and up.

events.title: Social Workers in the Library Drop-In Hours
events.description: Advice | Information | Referral. Social Workers in the Library offers free social service information and referrals*. Our staff can meet with you, approach your needs without judgement, and help you find where to go for shelter, food, showers, mental health services, legal help, and more. Free. No registration required. *Disclaimer: SJPL's Social Work in the Library does not establish a social worker-client relationship. SJPL does not offer case management or extensive follow-up services. We will try our best to get you connected to any resource we know of that could suit your needs. Tư Vấn / Thông Tin / Giới Thiệu Nhân Viên Xã Hội trong Thư Viện cung cấp miễn phí thông tin về những dịch vụ xã hội và giới thiệu. Nhân viên của chúng tôi có thể gặp gỡ bạn, tiếp cận với nhu cầu của bạn mà không đánh giá, và giúp bạn tìm những nơi để đến trú ẩn, thực phẩm, tắm rửa, những dịch vụ sức khoẻ tâm thần, trợ giúp pháp lý, và nhiều hơn nữa. Miễn phí. Không bắt buộc phải đăng ký. Từ chối trách nhiệm: Nhân Viên Xã Hội của SJPL trong Thư Viện không thiết lập mối quan hệ giữa một nhân viên xã hội và khách hàng. SJPL không cung cấp quản lý các trường hợp hoặc dịch vụ theo dõi mở rộng. Chúng tôi sẽ cố gắng hết sức để kết nối bạn với bất kỳ nguồn nào chúng tôi biết có thể phù hợp với nhu cầu của bạn. Asesoramiento | Información | Referencia. Este programa ofrece información y referencias de servicios sociales gratuitos. Nuestro personal puede reunirse con usted, abordar sus necesidades sin juicio y ayudarle a encontrar dónde ir para obtener refugio, comida, duchas, servicios de salud mental, ayuda legal y más. Gratis. No se requiere registro. *Aviso: El Trabajo Social en la Biblioteca de SJPL no establece una relación de Trabajador Social-Cliente. SJPL no ofrece gestión de casos ni servicios de seguimiento extensos. Haremos todo lo posible por conectarte con cualquier recurso que conozcamos y que pueda satisfacer tus necesidades.
events.blurb: Drop in to talk with a social worker and get free social service information and referrals.

events.title: Math Buddies
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Math Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their math skills by working one-on-one with a volunteer. At Math Buddies, volunteers sit with participating children for an individual, 15-20-minute tutoring session. Volunteers may help participants complete math homework assignments or math worksheet(s) provided by Math Buddies volunteers. Math Buddies creates a positive learning experience for students who may be struggling with math or lack confidence as math students. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, tutoring sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis, and the availability of sessions may be limited depending on the number of volunteers and/or participating children.

events.description: Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. events.title: Teens Reach
events.description: Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library for ages 13-18, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. events.title: ELL Advanced English: Writing Club
events.description: English Language Learners (ELL) can practice basic writing skills in English with our tutor in a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners. Topics may include creating simple sentence structures, learning some basic grammar, and building up to writing a simple paragraph. Suggested for high beginners up to advanced English language learners. Space is limited and registration is required. Please stop by the Vineland Library or call us at (408) 808-3000 to register. Vineland's English Learning series: ELL Beginning English: A beginner program for learners with limited English skills; approximately levels 0-2; ELL Grammar and Vocabulary Club: An intermediate program for learners that know some English but want to learn more complex English; approximately levels 2-3; ELL Conversation Club: An advanced program for learners to practice speaking and listening while also learning about American culture and idioms; approximately levels 3-4; ELL Writing Club: A program where high beginners to advanced level English language learners can learn and practice their English writing skills; approximately levels 2-4.

events.title: Mahjong Club
events.description: Adults and seniors who are interested in learning the basics or need a refresher on how to play Taiwanese Mahjong are welcome to join this program. You'll learn while playing the game: how to set up the game tiles and understand them; the flow of the game; making sets during the game; how to win. Learning Mahjong improves cognitive function, helps reduce stress and creates a sense of community. events.title: Creative Writing Workshop
events.description: Are you a budding creative writer? Whether you've written for years or started yesterday, register for fresh inspiration to make your story shine! Young writers in 2nd through 5th grade (ages 7-11) are invited to join us for this creative writing workshop series hosted at the Pearl Avenue Branch Library. Attendees will learn to: Write fiction that reads like reality; Create characters that leave readers breathless; Identify plot points that serve multiple genres. This series will run from Tuesday, May 5th to Tuesday, December 15th, 2026. Please register for each session of this workshop you are looking to attend. Free. Registration is required. This program is generously sponsored by the Pearl Avenue Friends of the Library.
events.blurb: Bring your work in progress and get fresh inspiration to sharpen your storytelling.

events.title: Digital Skills: One-On-One Tech Help for Seniors
events.description: Do you have questions or need assistance with technology? events.title: Homework Coaching with Delaney
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Need homework help? Students in kindergarten through 5th grade can meet with volunteer Homework Coach Delaney in the Children's Room to get homework support. Students must have assigned homework to work on to participate in a session. Homework Coaches can help look up and explain concepts covered on assigned homework, support students as they work through their assignments, check work, provide a set time to work on homework, and redirect focus as needed. events.title: 3D Printing One-on-One Appointment
events.description: Need help with 3D printing or looking for guided, hands-on experience? This session is ideal for beginners seeking practical experience, guided support, and confidence in using 3D printing technology. This is also a good opportunity for those who attended our 3D Design & Printing workshop and now want to try their hands at it. Participants will have the opportunity to print a simple model under supervision. If you do not have a design, you may choose a free design from Thingiverse or a similar site. All designs are printed in a single color of PLA - filament color at the discretion of the program lead. Designs must print in 1 hour 45 minutes - if you're not sure how long your design will take to print, email cz.sjpl@sjlibrary.org. SJPL reserves the right to refuse any print request. All designs must be compatible with the Creality K1C printer and have a print time of under 45 minutes. Final approval of printability will be determined by the program lead. One appointment per month per person.

events.blurb: Get one-on-one, hands-on guidance with 3D printing at Calabazas Library, a session aimed at beginners wanting practical experience.

Tiempo de Cuentos & Stay and Play: Tiempo de Cuentos está diseñado para niños pequeños e invita a toda la familia a participar en actividades de alfabetización temprana, como cuentos, rimas, juegos con los dedos y actividades de movimiento. Después de que concluya el Tiempo de Cuentos, las familias están invitadas a quedarse y jugar. Durante 30 minutos después del Tiempo de Cuentos, habrá juguetes especiales y apropiados para cada edad disponibles para continuar la diversión. events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and play with your toddler during this bilingual early literacy storytime.

events.title: Make & Decorate Sugar Skulls
events.description: Get ready for Día de los Muertos by making a sugar skull! In this multi-session program, participants will learn to make and then decorate sugar skulls using traditional and modern materials. In the first session, using a special sugar mixture and premade molds, we'll create the parts needed for a sugar skull. In the next session, after the sugar skulls have cured, we'll connect the sugar skull pieces and decorate them with colored frosting, foil, sequins, and more! Once decorated, the sugar skulls will be ready to display on your home altar or our community ofrenda. Please note: creating sugar skulls is a multi-day process. Participants will not be able to finish their skulls in one session and should plan to return for the second session to decorate skulls. Session 1: Sunday, November 1, 11:00 AM - 12:30 PM*; Session 2: Tuesday, November 3, 3:30 PM - 5:30 PM. *This program session will take place before the library opens to the public; participants will enter our community room through the doors adjacent to the parking lot. **Sugar skulls not claimed after the program will be discarded. ¡Haz & decora tu propia Calaverita de Azúcar! ¡Ven a celebrar el Día de los Muertos creando una calaverita de azúcar muy especial! En este divertido programa de varias sesiones, aprenderás a hacer y decorar calaveritas usando materiales tradicionales y modernos. En la primera sesión, usaremos una mezcla especial de azúcar y moldes para formar las piezas de la calaverita. En la siguiente sesión, cuando ya estén listas y duritas, uniremos las piezas y las decoraremos con papel de colores, lentejuelas, pintura y mucho más. Al final, podrás llevarte tu calaverita para ponerla en tu altar en casa o en la ofrenda de la comunidad. Importante: Las calaveritas necesitan varios días para estar listas, así que no podrás terminar todo en una sola sesión. ¡Planea regresar a las siguientes para decorarlas! Sesión 1: Domingo, 1 de noviembre, 11:00 - 12:30 PM; Sesión 2: Martes, 3 de noviembre, 3:30 - 5:30 PM
events.blurb: Make and decorate your own sugar skull with traditional and modern materials in a multi-session Día de los Muertos program.

events.title: Sci-Fi & Fantasy Book Club
events.description: Join us to read The Cyberiad by Stanislaw Lem. You can register for the club and get a copy of the book at the adult reference desk. "Trurl and Klapaucius are 'constructors'; they travel around the universe creating machines of astonishing inventiveness and power and visiting a bewildering variety of violent, peculiar and morose civilizations. The Cyberiad is oddly reminiscent of Gulliver's Travels, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, The Phantom Tollbooth and Alice in Wonderland. Charming, mind-bending and anarchic, it is perhaps Lem's greatest work. This edition includes all of Daniel Mroz's hallucinatory original illustrations." For accessibility accommodations (ex. events.title: Peter Fletcher Classical Guitar Concert
events.description: Please join us for a performance by classical guitarist Peter Fletcher, with a program titled "Music of Four Centuries." events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, TransMilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at SXSW and received critical acclaim. TransMilitary was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, SideXSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to SideXSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch this documentary tracing a Stasi victim's personal investigation into East Germany's surveillance machine.

events.title: Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion: Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea
events.description: In November, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea by Barbara Demick (2009). The book is based on Demick's interviews over a seven-year period with six North Koreans who escaped the country and the regime. The vast majority of North Koreans know little more of the world beyond their borders than the rest of the world knows about their daily lives under the Kim Jong-il regime. Without easy access to healthcare, experiencing frequent food shortages, life for the average working family in North Korea under Kim Jong-Il's rule is and was grim by Western standards. As of the publication date of this book, ordinary citizens have few if any civil rights and almost no recourse to protest injustice, as complaints and almost any sign of dissatisfaction with the regime could lead to imprisonment. The adult Non-Fiction book group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Documentaries: Holodomor Remembrance Day
events.description: The Holodomor, the famine that killed millions of Ukrainians in the 1930s, was not widely known or acknowledged until the fall of the Soviet Union in the 1990s. Established in 1998, Holodomor Remembrance Day is observed on the fourth Saturday of November to remember those who died during the Holodomor. Join us for Palo Alto City Library's second annual program commemorating this event and its lasting effects for some in our community today. Three short documentaries will give us the historical background that reverberates in current events. Descriptions of the documentaries below were written by their creators. Holodomor: How Millions of Ukrainians Died of Starvation During Stalin-Era Mass Famine (Radio Free Europe, 2019, two minutes). Each year, on the fourth Saturday of November, Ukraine remembers the millions who died during the Holodomor, the Stalin-era famine that devastated the population in 1932-1933. Many countries consider it to have been genocide. Minnesota Memories of the Holodomor (PBS, 2025, 26 minutes). In an extraordinary exploration of the transmission of traumatic memory within families, communities and across generations, Ukrainians in Minneapolis-St. Paul share their family stories about the Holodomor artificial famine of 1932-33 and the local community's efforts to come to terms with genocide, even as war once again threatens the existence of Ukrainians as a people. Holodomor: Voices of Survivors (2015, 30 minutes). Twenty-five Ukrainian Canadians tell their stories of survival during the Holodomor--death inflicted by starvation--a genocide of Ukrainian people engineered by Joseph Stalin during 1932 and 1933. Through compelling eyewitness accounts, the film brings into focus a pivotal and little-known period in history, the consequences of which continue to reverberate today. Books on this reading list will be on display and available. Registration is not necessary, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

(There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? events.title: Medicare: Enrollment, 2027 Updates and Plan Review Tips
events.description: The Medicare Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) runs from October 15 through December 7 each year. During this time, Medicare beneficiaries can review and make changes to their Medicare health and prescription drug coverage for the coming year. Join HICAP (Health Insurance Counseling & Advocacy Program) for a free educational presentation covering Medicare updates taking effect in 2027, Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review strategies, and important factors to consider when evaluating your coverage options. Learn how to compare plan costs, provider networks, prescription drug coverage, and other benefits to determine whether your current plan continues to meet your needs. Following the presentation, HICAP counselors will be available for free one-on-one counseling sessions to answer Medicare questions and help attendees review their coverage options. HICAP counselors are unbiased and are not affiliated with any insurance company. The one-on-one sessions will be on a first-come, first-served basis. HICAP is a program of Sourcewise providing free Medicare counseling to Santa Clara County residents. Who Should Attend? Current Medicare beneficiaries reviewing their coverage for 2027; Individuals approaching Medicare eligibility; Family members and caregivers assisting a Medicare beneficiary. What You Will Learn: Medicare updates taking effect in 2027; How the Annual Enrollment Period works; Medicare Advantage and Part D plan review tips; How to compare costs, coverage, and provider networks; Prescription drug coverage considerations; When it may make sense to change plans; Resources and assistance available through HICAP. What to Bring: A complete list of your prescription medications, including dosage and quantity, for accurate plan comparisons. Your Medicare card (optional, but helpful). HICAP counselors will have laptops available for Medicare plan reviews, but attendees are welcome to bring their own laptop or tablet. Time Required: The time needed to complete a plan comparison varies depending on the number of prescriptions and coverage options being reviewed. Most plan reviews take approximately 30–60 minutes. This program is intended for Santa Clara County residents. Please register if you would like to receive a reminder about the presentation. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org. About Sourcewise: Since 1973, Sourcewise has provided services and support to seniors in Santa Clara County. Sourcewise aims to inform, educate, and prepare all adults within Santa Clara County to better navigate their health and life options.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep them on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear author Dr. Carol Peyser speak at an evening author event at Rinconada Library.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY.), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post); "outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... provocative.... moving.... beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film but national PBS, however, has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick MacArthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary on Panama and discuss its themes of militarization.
