events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Ukraine: Culture, Geography, History and Heritage
events.description: Nora Mason, a native-born Ukrainian and long-time Saratoga resident, will present a program on the culture of Ukraine and how its geography has contributed to tragic invasions over time. She will share her family's WWII story and how they ultimately immigrated to the United States. She will also touch on inspiring efforts to help the people of Ukraine today. Program co-sponsored by the Los Gatos-Saratoga AAUW.
events.blurb: Hear Ukrainian-born Saratoga resident Nora Mason talk about Ukraine's culture and how its geography has shaped its history of invasions.

events.description: California Writers Club-San Francisco Peninsula Branch members share their expertise on writing, editing, marketing, publishing and more. Writers Helping Writers resumes for its fourth year on the third Thursday of these months: October 15; January 21; March 18; May 20. Registration is not required, but if you register, you'll receive an email reminder the day before the event.
events.blurb: Hear California Writers Club members share advice on writing, editing, marketing and publishing at this Thursday evening session.

events.title: Poetry Open Mic
events.description: Come share poetry. Come hear poetry. You do not have to be a poet to attend! Presented by Poetry Los Altos. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Share your own poems or just listen at Los Altos Library's open mic hosted by Poetry Los Altos.

events.title: Teen Rubik's Cube Club
events.description: Meet other cubers, learn new techniques, and have fun! Snacks and drinks provided. For ages 12+. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility at least 7 days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Swap cube-solving techniques with fellow cubers while snacking on provided treats.

Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!

events.title: Lego Club!
events.description: Come join us every Sunday for Lego Club! We have tons of Lego bricks for you to build and explore! Duplo bricks are also available for our younger friends. Want to push yourself and try something a little more difficult? Ask the librarian for a Lego Challenge! Important: Children under 5 must be accompanied by their parents as small LEGO pieces can be choking hazards.
events.blurb: Build with a huge collection of Lego and Duplo bricks and try a librarian-issued Lego Challenge.

events.title: ELL (English Language Learner) Conversation Club
events.description: This program is held in person at Santa Teresa Branch Library. English Language Learners (ELL) Conversation Clubs create a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English conversation skills. Clubs meet weekly with a trained facilitator courtesy of Santa Teresa Branch Library. No registration required. Materials will be provided.
events.blurb: Practice English conversation with other adult learners in a welcoming, in-person club at Santa Teresa Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Family Craft: Bean and Lentil Mosaics
events.description: Choose from a variety of beans and lentils to create your own colorful mosaic! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using paper, glue, beans, and lentils. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Design a colorful mosaic from beans and lentils in this hands-on family craft session.

events.title: TeenHQ: Pipe Cleaner Flowers
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Come hang out in TeenHQ and create fun and long-lasting flower bouquets out of pipe cleaners. This event takes place in TeenHQ and is for Middle and High Schoolers (grades 6-12) only. Adults and younger relations can wait for teens in the TeenHQ Reading Room. Parking at King Library: It is recommended to park at the 4th Street Garage. The first 90 minutes are free.
events.blurb: Make pipe cleaner flower bouquets in TeenHQ at King Library, an afternoon session for grades 6-12.

events.title: Chair Yoga with Patricia Becker
events.description: Join established local yoga teacher Patricia Becker as she takes us through exercises to loosen joints, improve flexibility, improve cognition, and increase strength in Rinconada Library's Embarcadero Room. Registration isn't needed but means you will receive an email reminder. Here are the dates for 2027: January 2; March 6; May 1; July 3; September 4; November 6.
events.attendanceNote: Registration is not required. Optional signup provides an email reminder.
events.blurb: Move through seated stretches with Patricia Becker to loosen joints and build strength in the Embarcadero Room.

events.title: Knitting / Crocheting / Tatting / Bobbin Lace Club
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Do you enjoy working with knitting, crocheting, or tatting? Do you want to learn how, see what others are working on, refine your skills, or talk about all kinds of hand needle crafts? Join us in the East San Jose Carnegie Branch Community Room every week. Everyone 7 and up is invited to participate, and younger children are welcome to accompany their families.
events.blurb: Bring your knitting, crocheting, or tatting project to work alongside other crafters and swap tips.

events.title: Halloween Festival
events.description: Join us for a special Halloween Festival at the Joyce Ellington Branch Library! There will be a Halloween-themed storytime, a parade with a chance for trick-or-treating throughout the library and an assortment of grab-and-go arts and crafts to choose from that are suitable for all ages. Please wear your costumes, if possible! Free. Registration not required.
events.blurb: Join the Halloween Festival at Joyce Ellington Library on a Saturday afternoon with your family.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Join Librarian Heidi on Friday mornings at 10:30 AM for Family Storytime at Downtown Library. Come sing, rhyme, and read stories with us! While this storytime will be geared towards those older than 2 years, all ages are welcome! Make sure to follow us on YouTube for more stories, songs and rhymes, including a playlist of all of our favorite songs to sing!
events.blurb: Sing, rhyme, and hear stories with Librarian Heidi at Family Storytime on Friday mornings.

events.title: Freaky Friday Night Flicks
events.description: Watch some Halloween classics at your library! Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid-back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. The library will provide popcorn, candy, and drinks. This program is for teens (ages 13-18). October 16th: Beetlejuice (1988); October 23rd: The Addams Family (1991); October 30th: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993).
events.blurb: Watch Halloween classics with popcorn, candy, and drinks provided at Campbell Library.

events.title: Game Zone
events.description: Are you an expert at video, board, and card games? Do you want to demonstrate your skills, or just want to learn the basics? Or maybe you'd like to sink the 8 ball at a game of pool? Join us in the Teen Room at the Hillview Branch Library if you want to play video, board, and card games, play some pool, or just hang out! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Play video, board, and card games in the Teen Room, or challenge friends to a game of pool.

events.title: Origami is Coding
events.description: Learn key concepts in coding through origami, the art of folding paper. Participants will fold a different animal or object each month. The techniques for folding the project will be tied to key concepts in coding. This is a completely unplugged activity that teaches computational reasoning without the use of a computer. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Fold paper animals while learning coding concepts in this unplugged origami session.

events.title: Family Craft: Pom Pom Photo Frames
events.description: Create and decorate a pom pom photo frame! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using popsicle sticks, glue, sequins, buttons, and pom poms. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.
events.blurb: Decorate a pom pom photo frame with your child using popsicle sticks and sequins at the Children's Library.

events.title: Reading to Children with Kathy
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Sit down with a volunteer reader for one-on-one or small group storytime that builds imagination and a love of books.

events.title: Reading to Children with Aysha
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. Kids are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Reading to Children will take place in the Children's Area.
events.blurb: Read one-on-one or in a small group with volunteer Aysha to build reading confidence and love of books.

events.title: Crochet Together
events.description: Crochet Together with the Mt Pleasant Neighborhood Library! Crochet Together is a volunteer-run event teaching participants how to crochet. Participants are welcome to bring their own materials. For children interested in crochet, the recommended age is 10 years old and older. Children who are 10 years old and younger must be accompanied by parents.
events.blurb: Learn to crochet with volunteer instructors, bringing your own materials if you have them.

events.title: Native American Heritage Storytime
events.description: Join us for an enriching celebration of Native American Heritage Month during our special storytime at the library. Immerse yourself in captivating tales and engaging activities that honor Native American communities' diverse cultures, traditions, and contributions. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Listen to stories and join activities honoring the cultures, traditions, and contributions of Native American communities during this library storytime for Native American Heritage Month.

events.title: Medicare Mysteries Solved!
events.description: Are you getting ready to apply for Medicare and are confused by the different plans to choose from? Join Sandra Karol, MS, RDMS, RVT, for a monthly workshop and learn more about the different plans that will work best for you and your family. Please register directly with Sandy at isail2@earthlink.net. Attendee limit is 10 people per session.
events.blurb: Learn about Medicare plan options from Sandra Karol in this monthly workshop.

events.title: Seven Trees Overfelt Adult Education ESL Class
events.description: Free. Placement test and registration required. Learn basic reading, writing, speaking, & listening skills with your library for free! This class meets in person at the Seven Trees Branch Library and is led by a certified English instructor in collaboration with Overfelt Adult Education Center at no cost. Call the library at (408) 808-3056.
events.blurb: Build basic English reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills in a free Overfelt Adult Education class, with a placement test and registration required.

events.title: Mandarin Storytime
events.description: Join us for fun stories, rhymes, fingerplays and songs in Mandarin! For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Hear stories, rhymes, fingerplays, and songs performed in Mandarin at this Saratoga Library storytime.

events.title: Arts & Crafts Fun
events.description: Our partner, Budding Leaders, is hosting arts and crafts classes for ages 4+ with adult help, 8+ solo. We will supply materials and samples and help you create beautiful artwork. Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.attendanceNote: Tickets available at the desk 30 minutes before the program starts. All individuals (of any age) attending need a ticket and must be present to receive their ticket.
events.blurb: Make artwork at a Budding Leaders craft class for ages 4 and up, with materials and samples supplied.

events.title: Sunday Game Day
events.description: We welcome children, teens, adults, and families to play a variety of board games and card games at the Edenvale Branch Library, every first Sunday of the month. There will be a mix of strategy-based games and educational games. A library staff member or volunteer will be available to explain game rules, as needed. Join in on the fun!
events.blurb: Play board games and card games with other families at the Edenvale branch on a Sunday afternoon.

events.title: Monthly Chat with Mayor Moore
events.description: Get ready to talk about what matters most to you. Mayor Kitty Moore is hosting a Monthly Chat Series in Cupertino throughout 2026, inviting residents and local businesses to discuss any topic with one of the City's decision-makers. These informal gatherings offer a welcoming space for meaningful conversation and community connection.
events.blurb: Sit down with Mayor Kitty Moore and raise whatever's on your mind at this informal monthly chat.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy a small group interaction with our volunteer. The program will be held under the Read to Children sign within the Children's Area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Join a volunteer for a small-group reading session in Berryessa Library's Children's Area.

events.title: Game On at the Library
events.description: Join us every Sunday at 1:00 p.m. at the Joyce Ellington Branch for a fun afternoon of board games! Choose from our large selection of games, including exciting new favorites and classic games that are fun for all ages. Bring your family and friends, roll the dice, and enjoy some friendly competition! No registration required.
events.blurb: Choose from a large selection of board games and play with family and friends at the library.

events.title: Classic Horror Movie Night
events.description: Start your Halloween off with the right vibes (spooky)! Join us at the Library to watch the classic horror film Poltergeist (1982). Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid-back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. The library will provide popcorn, candy, and drinks. While this film is rated PG, we recommend ages 16+.
events.blurb: Watch the classic horror film Poltergeist with popcorn, candy, and drinks provided by the library.

events.title: Board Game Zone
events.description: Join us every Sunday between 2:00 and 4:00 PM at the Seven Trees Library to play fun board games! We have a large selection to choose from, including new games and classic games that everyone of all ages can enjoy. No registration required. Thanks to the Friends of the Seven Trees Library for making this possible!
events.blurb: Play board games from a large selection of new and classic titles at Seven Trees Library, with no registration required.

events.title: Music & Storytelling with Kirk Waller
events.description: Join us for a performance with musician and storyteller Kirk Waller! Kirk mesmerizes audiences of all ages with a dynamic blend of music, movement, and storytelling. Journey with him through captivating tales from long ago and far away, brought vividly to life through his energetic and engaging performance style.
events.blurb: Watch musician and storyteller Kirk Waller mix music, movement, and stories in a performance for audiences of all ages.

events.title: Friday Fun (Grab & Go): Fall Animals Diamond Painting Keychains
events.description: This week, we'll make diamond painting keychains featuring several designs of adorable animals with an autumn theme. This will be a grab-and-go format. All supplies will be provided. Free. No registration required. For ages 6 and up. Explore more Friday Fun at Tully Community Branch events on our events calendar.
events.blurb: Make an autumn animal diamond painting keychain in a grab-and-go craft session with supplies provided, for ages 6 and up.

events.title: Financial Health and Wellness: Optimizing Social Security Benefits
events.description: Join the Library as we welcome financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada of the Heartland Institute of Financial Education back for a workshop series on financial health and wellness! Registration opens two weeks before the event date and is preferred for each individual session to adequately accommodate seating.
events.blurb: Hear financial wellness instructor Brad Hamada explain strategies for optimizing your Social Security benefits.

events.title: Excel Basics
events.description: New to Microsoft Excel? This beginner-friendly workshop will introduce you to the essentials, including navigating spreadsheets, entering and formatting data, creating simple formulas, and organizing information. Get comfortable with Excel and build the skills you need to confidently tackle everyday tasks. Free.
events.blurb: Learn to navigate spreadsheets, enter data, and build simple formulas in this beginner Excel workshop.

events.title: Celebrate Native American Heritage Month! Story and Craft
events.description: Join Librarian Jennifer as we celebrate Native American Heritage Month! We'll be sharing Native American folk tales, then crafting traditional clay pinch pots. Please note that while all ages are welcome, this program is designed for children ages 5 and up. Space and supplies are limited; please arrive on time!
events.blurb: Hear Native American folk tales and craft a clay pinch pot at Palo Alto's Children's Library.

events.title: ESL Conversation Club for English Language Learners (ELL)
events.description: Practice and improve your English-speaking skills in a group setting with a volunteer facilitator, discussing a variety of topics. A basic understanding of English is required. The purpose of this group is to help learners practice speaking and build confidence and comfort when communicating in English.
events.blurb: Build confidence speaking English with a volunteer facilitator at Joyce Ellington Library's conversation club.

events.title: Crochet Club
events.description: All are welcome—from beginners to experienced enthusiasts. Bring your own project or start a new one as we refine our skills and discuss all things crochet. events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!); Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Celebrate Diwali with the community at Mitchell Park Community Center's Festival of Lights.

events.title: Cielo Hotel Valencia Rooftop Holiday Experience
events.description: November 27, 2026. Beginning November 27, join us Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00–9:00 pm, for winter evenings at Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia. The experience will be closed Sundays and Mondays. This holiday season, Cielo Rooftop transforms into an intimate winter retreat high above Santana Row, where seasonal warmth and elevated style come together against the backdrop of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Settle in beneath the open sky and enjoy seasonal cocktails and a curated menu of winter-inspired bites in a warm and inviting rooftop setting. Thoughtful seasonal touches and the glow of the city below create the perfect atmosphere for festive gatherings, date nights, or simply savoring the season.
events.blurb: Spend a winter evening on the Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia, open Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00 to 9:00 pm.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. No partner needed and beginners welcome! You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you will get an email reminder for the program including a link to the class playlist to practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps with Sandy and Kent to international music; no partner or experience needed.

events.title: Location Change: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Join Phuong Pham for a mindfulness meditation session at the Art Center Meeting Room.

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk along Stevens Creek with a naturalist to learn about the Steelhead life cycle and riparian habitat.

events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! *This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shouldered Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the riparian trails with Park Rangers on Saturday morning, learning to identify local birds and watching for hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.

events.description: Curated by Associate Curator of European Art Patrick R. Crowley, Jane! celebrates the aesthetic and affective excesses of Jane Stanford, the Gilded Age founder and matriarch of Stanford University.

events.title: Electric Contrasts: the Art of the Detail

events.title: Korean Indigenous Futures: The Art of Kim Bong-Jun

events.title: Emergent Properties: Decennial Reflections on Collections

events.title: Something Sensational to Read: A Tour of Silicon Valley LGBTQ+ Publications, 1950 to Today
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St, San Jose, CA 95112
events.blurb: Tour a collection of Silicon Valley LGBTQ+ publications spanning 1950 to today at King Library.

events.title: Downtown Palo Alto Farmers' Market
events.venue: Gilman Street between Hamilton and Forest
events.address: Gilman Street between Hamilton and Forest, Palo Alto
events.description: The Downtown Palo Alto Farmers' Market runs Saturday, October 31, from 8 AM to noon on Gilman Street between Hamilton and Forest. Gaby Castro's music set starts at 9:30 AM.
events.blurb: Browse the Downtown Palo Alto Farmers' Market and hear music by Gaby Castro.

events.title: Artist Reception & Gallery Talk with Zoe Caron
events.address: MVCPA SecondStage, 500 Castro St, Mountain View, CA 94041
events.description: A free artist reception and gallery talk featuring Bay Area artist Zoe Caron, exploring high-contrast realism and the natural world as part of the Nature's Pulse exhibition; doors open at 5:00 PM with the talk beginning at 6:00 PM.
events.blurb: Meet Bay Area artist Zoe Caron and hear her discuss high-contrast realism at the Nature's Pulse gallery talk.

events.title: Triton Book Club: The Last Tycoon
events.address: Triton Museum of Art, 1505 Warburton Avenue, Santa Clara, CA 95050
events.description: Book club discussion of F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Last Tycoon, led by Triton Curator Vanessa Callanta, who traces the history of filmmaking. Free for members, $5 suggested donation for non-members.
events.blurb: Discuss F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Last Tycoon with Triton Curator Vanessa Callanta, who traces the history of filmmaking.

events.title: Let's Work! Quarry Park Clean-Up
events.description: Volunteer workday kicking off the winter Let's Work! Program, removing non-native invasive plants from Quarry Park. Volunteers must be 15+ or ages 10-14 with an adult, and registration is required.
events.blurb: Pull non-native invasive plants from Quarry Park with fellow volunteers; registration is required, and ages 10-14 need an adult.
events.attendanceNote: Volunteers must be at least 15 to participate independently; ages 10–14 need an accompanying adult volunteer. Registration closes three days before the workday or when full.

events.title: Repair Café
events.address: Sunnyvale Public Library, Library Program Room
events.description: Bring a broken item and get one-on-one help fixing it. First-come, first-served, limit two items per household, and the last new fix is at 2 p.m.
events.blurb: Bring a broken item for one-on-one help fixing it at the Repair Café, limited to two items per household, first-come, first-served.

events.title: Theology on Tap
events.address: Hapa's Brewing Company, 114 S Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos
events.description: Pastor Dave from the Presbyterian Church of Los Gatos hosts a casual theological discussion over drinks. Ages 21 and up.
events.blurb: Join Pastor Dave for a casual theological discussion over drinks at Hapa's Brewing Company, open to ages 21 and up.

events.title: PCLG Christmas Tea
events.address: Presbyterian Church of Los Gatos, 16575 Shannon Rd, Los Gatos
events.description: Annual Christmas Tea with a performance by the Mountain View High School Madrigal Choir in the sanctuary, followed by homemade treats in the Social Hall. Tickets are $25, sold after Sunday worship (cash or check).
events.blurb: Hear the Mountain View High School Madrigal Choir in the sanctuary, then enjoy homemade treats in the Social Hall; tickets are $25.

events.title: Puzzle Swap
events.address: Lobby, Mountain View Senior Center, 266 Escuela Ave., Mountain View, CA 94040
events.description: Bring a puzzle or two and swap them for puzzles from the Senior Center at no charge. No registration needed.
events.blurb: Swap a puzzle or two from home for new ones in the Mountain View Senior Center lobby. No registration needed.

events.title: Hysterical: Mary Lynn Rajskub
events.description: Comedian and actress Mary Lynn Rajskub, known for '24' and 'It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia,' performs stand-up exploring modern womanhood.
events.blurb: Watch comedian Mary Lynn Rajskub, known for '24' and 'It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia,' riff on modern womanhood.
